newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul gold prices rise, volume drops.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul gold prices rise, volume drops.

text.p: Istanbul gold prices rose slightly to $379.70 an ounce from Monday's $379.25 in line with firmer levels in Europe.
Traded volume further eased to 703 kilos from Monday's 862 due to weak demand, dealers said.
Gold jumped to 1,192,250 lira per gram from Monday's 1,184,000 lira, buoyed by the weakness of the Turkish lira against the dollar in the domestic currency market.
The lira closed sharply lower at 97,340 to the dollar versus Monday's 96,850 due to expectations of lira surplus on Wednesday following a surprisingly low sale in today's Treasury-bill auction.
Dealers said rising gold prices in lira fuelled trade in lira terms, which accounted for 77 percent of the total.
Trading was more even on Tuesday with 323 kilos traded in the morning and 380 in the afternoon.
Dealers said volume was unusually high in the afternoon session, when the lira weakened sharply against the dollar in reaction to the auction results.
